question: Should the CLI/core URL extractor support Reddit threads directly, and if so should it use an unauthenticated `.json` path plus explicit blocked-page errors rather than browser credentials?
rationale: The code fix is not only mechanical: authenticated browser extraction, public Reddit JSON, Firecrawl, and fail-fast diagnostics have different privacy, dependency, and support tradeoffs.

options.title: Core-safe Reddit support
options.body: Add a CLI/core Reddit thread extractor for public `.json` responses and emit a clear blocked-site diagnostic when Reddit returns verification content.

options.title: Guidance-only CLI boundary
options.body: Keep CLI extraction generic and document Chrome extension or Firecrawl as the supported workaround for Reddit verification pages.

options.title: Browser-authenticated path
options.body: Explore a broader browser-cookie or extension-mediated CLI flow, accepting the larger privacy and support surface.

recommendation.title: Core-safe Reddit support
recommendation.body: Add a CLI/core Reddit thread extractor for public `.json` responses and emit a clear blocked-site diagnostic when Reddit returns verification content.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision affects the core CLI extraction boundary and Peter Steinberger is the recent owner of that path in git history.
